metaData.originalTitle: Superpowers：给 Claude Code 装上“工程大脑”
metaData.title: Superpowers: Giving Claude Code an "Engineering Brain"
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the Superpowers project, explaining how it imposes engineering discipline on Claude Code through 14 built-in skills, transforming AI coding from probabilistic free-form output into a deterministic, reproducible engineering process.
metaData.summary: The article begins with the author's pain points with AI coding encountered in the querit.ai project, pointing out three original sins of running Claude Code bare: response randomness, intuitive fast thinking, and attention dilution. It then introduces the Superpowers project, detailing the background of its author Jesse Vincent, the project's origin, phenomenal growth data, and official recognition from Anthropic. The core of the article deeply dissects Superpowers' 14 core skills, overall workflow, and Skill file structure. Using the brainstorming skill as an example, through source code analysis and comparative experiments, it demonstrates how techniques like mandatory instructions, structural templates, state locking, and chained calls alter the LLM's probability distribution, turning AI from a free-spirited artist into a disciplined engineer. The article also explores the relationship between Superpowers and "The Bitter Lesson," arguing they are not in competition at the same level, and predicts that when the model's intrinsic capabilities fill the discipline gap, such external add-ons will be phased out. Finally, the article reviews the querit.ai subscription payment frontend case, comparing the development workflow differences before and after using Superpowers.

mainPoints.point: What AI coding agents lack is not capability, but discipline.
mainPoints.explanation: Native Claude Code tends to output code directly, easily missing key steps like requirement clarification, boundary handling, and testing, leading to unstable results and numerous bugs. Superpowers solves this by enforcing process constraints.

mainPoints.point: Superpowers constrains AI behavior by altering the LLM's probability distribution.
mainPoints.explanation: Through system prompt injection, it significantly increases the probability of correct behaviors like 'clarify requirements first, design a plan,' transforming AI from probabilistic free-form sampling into engineering execution following a deterministic process.

mainPoints.point: Superpowers' design philosophy is 'manage an AI agent like managing a junior developer.'
mainPoints.explanation: Author Jesse Vincent applies 30 years of experience managing development teams to AI agents, ensuring consistency and reliability of AI output by defining clear processes, enforcing validation, and state locking.

mainPoints.point: Superpowers and 'The Bitter Lesson' are not contradictory; they operate on different levels.
mainPoints.explanation: 'The Bitter Lesson' discusses how to make models smarter, while Superpowers discusses how to make an already smart model consistently exhibit desired behavior in a given task. It is an art of process management in human-computer collaboration.

keyQuotes: What AI coding agents lack is not capability, but discipline.
Superpowers doesn't make AI smarter; it makes AI disciplined.
Impose the same discipline a senior engineering manager would on a junior developer: stop, think, plan, then build.
Superpowers is not about 'teaching Claude how to design,' but 'forcing Claude to follow a design process.'

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: Browser Use: Building a Runtime Harness for Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build an open-source tool based on the Chrome DevTools Protocol that enables AI agents to operate real browsers for multi-dimensional verification—including visual, interactive, and console checks—thereby ensuring the delivery quality of web products.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: Enabling Coding Agents to Reliably Complete Long-Horizon Tasks
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article introduces the Harness Engineering framework, which addresses the reliability challenges of Coding Agents in large-scale, long-horizon tasks through task decomposition, parallel scheduling, File-as-Progress state persistence, and multi-layered retry mechanisms.

relatedArticles.title: After Reading the Claude Code Source Code, I Realized: The Differences Between Skills, MCP, and Rules Are Not as Big as You Think
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article, through an in-depth analysis of the leaked Claude Code source code, reveals the underlying implementation mechanisms of the three concepts—Rules, MCP, and Skills—pointing out that their core difference lies in where information is injected within the API request, and provides practical advice based on insights from the source code.

relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: How I Spent a Week Boosting AI Coding Rate to 90% in an Enterprise App
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces Harness Engineering, a new AI coding paradigm that elevates the AI code rate of an enterprise Java application from 25% to over 90% by building a four-element system of rules, skills, knowledge, and change management.
